thread:
Marco: Heads up — trying to onboard `pinecone-2.7b` from the model-registry. License file says 'NonCommercial‑Attribution v1'. Can we include this on Dedicated or ship quantized weights to customers?

Rachel (Legal): short answer: probably not for commercial offerings. 'NonCommercial' typically forbids commercial exploitation. Need to see full text, but hosting as a paid API or distributing weights to paying customers is risky. Drop the license link.

Marco: link: https://models.example/pinecone-2.7b/LICENSE.txt

Iona: quick tech Q — our quantization step converts weights and changes dtype/layout (q4_0 style). Does that count as a derivative? Example command we run: `python tools/quantize.py --in model.safetensors --bits 4 --out pinecone-2.7b-q4.tar.gz`

Rachel (Legal): modifying the weights is usually treated as creating a derivative. Many OS-style licenses that add a NonCommercial clause also treat transformed binaries as covered. So even if you only ship a quantized version, that's redistribution of derivative material.

Sam (Product): what about Private deployments where customer infra pulls the upstream model and runs our quantize script locally? We wouldn't be shipping the weights in that flow. Is that acceptable?

Rachel (Legal): if the customer downloads directly from the upstream provider themselves and we only provide the orchestration code (no binary), the legal risk to Redwood is much lower — because we're not redistributing the model. However: 1) we must make that explicit in our installer and docs, 2) include a required customer attestation (contract clause) that they have the rights to use the model commercially, and 3) require attribution per the license text.

Iona: noted. So recommended onboarding policy for now:
- Hosted API: blocked until we secure a commercial license or permission from the model author.
- Dedicated (Redwood-provided weights): blocked.
- Private (customer‑managed infra): allowed only if the installer downloads from upstream and customer signs attestation + we surface attribution in the UI/docs.

Marco: OK I'll flip the model-catalog flag: `license_blocker: true` and add this thread link. I'll also add a note to the onboarding PR.

deploy-bot: Model scan completed: LICENSE detected: 'NonCommercial-Attribution v1' — flagged for legal review. :warning:

Rachel (Legal): I'll draft an email template to request a commercial/enterprise license from Pinecone Labs and capture the required attribution text. Also will prepare a 1‑pager compliance checklist for onboarding (license type, attribution, redistribution allowed?, commercial use?).

Sam (Product): thanks — can you cc sales on the template? a few prospects asked specifically for this model.

Rachel (Legal): will do. For immediate next steps: Marco, please pause any Hosted/Dedicated rollout, update model-catalog entry with license link, and add an onboarding ticket for Legal to own the outreach.

Marco: done — ticket created: models#7823. I'll tag @sales once legal has the template.

Iona: would be great to have an automated check in the CI that fails onboarding if license contains 'NonCommercial' or 'NoCommercial' keywords. I can add a quick rule to the model-registry CI.

Rachel (Legal): yes pls — that would prevent accidental hostings. Add me as reviewer.

Sam (Product): perfect. closing for now, we can re-open after legal outreach. :thumbsup:
